prompt:
Fantasy trading-card illustration in the style of early-to-mid 1990s card art: hand-made traditional media (gouache, acrylic, watercolour and pen-and-ink), visible brushstrokes and pen lines, matte paper texture, and the slightly soft, faded look of a card printed in the 1990s. Expressive and a little stylised rather than realistic: strong shapes, bold silhouettes, sometimes inked outlines and flat patterned colour. Dark overall with near-black shadows, lit by bold, saturated accent colours (ember orange, deep violet, sea teal, deep crimson) where they matter. Frame the subject tightly: it fills most of the picture and may be cropped by the edges, with its face or focal point near the centre; keep the background minimal, simple and dark. Landscape 3:2 composition. No text, no letters, no border, no card frame, no logo, no watermark, no signature. Not photorealistic, not 3D render, not modern digital concept art, not anime.

Setting: Greek myth as told in Homer, Hesiod and the Greek tragedies, depicted faithfully to those stories: bronze armour, crested helmets, round aspis shields, linen chitons, black ships, the wine-dark Aegean sea, white limestone, temples, cypress, smoke and fire.

Subject: Iphigenia, daughter of Agamemnon, standing calmly at the altar at Aulis in a white robe as the goddess Artemis spirits her away and a deer appears in her place in a burst of light, the becalmed fleet behind.

Composition: a close-up of Iphigenia's calm face under a white veil, the glowing eyes of a deer behind her. Light and colour: soft divine white light. Presence: larger than life, monumental and iconic, with divine golden rim light; the most dramatic kind of image in the set. The subject fills most of the picture; keep the background minimal.
